c.st: Steven Weinberg: Science books for the general reader
c.x:

  The Elegant Universe (1999) Brian Greene
  The Selfish Gene (1976) Richard Dawkins

c.st: Ask HN: Who are your favorite poets?
c.x:
Favourite? I don't know... Blake? Poe? Various Japanese classics? Currently reading "Paradise Lost" by Milton. But what I've probably listened to most, lately, is Kate Tempest:

    I know now, first hand,
    That regretting love will empty you
    Of all that makes you love
    And all that lovers pay attention to.

    (Verse from "Best Intentions", Kate Tempest)

It's interesting to see that many seem to have fallen in love with poetry that's been translated to English. While there's nothing wrong with…

c.st: Ask HN: What are you reading?
c.x:
There's a lovely and eccentric quiz show on the BBC called Only Connect. Last year the host as part of her bit to fill time tried to fill it with reading excerpts from Paradise Lost. It was funny, and the in-joke I think was to remind us all of what Samuel Johnson once said of it:

> "Paradise Lost is one of the books which the reader admires and lays down, and forgets to take up again. None ever wished it longer than it is."

"working through it" does indeed seem like the right phrasing from what little I've been…
